By the strictest definition, yes, downvoats are censorship. The difference here is that allowing the community to decide what gets more views and what never sees daylight gives the practice a "logical" leg to stand on. Users reason, "If the community decided to censor material, in a democratic fashion, then perhaps it should be censored." Yes, this line of thinking falls into a logical fallacy. A popular position is not always the right position.

The alternative is top-down censorship, where an individual arbitrarily decides what can and cannot be viewed by the community. Asking the community to accept the judgement of multiple users, versus the judgement of one administrator, allows a site to keep an active user base, because they are given some power.

The real world equivalent would be the comparison between a democracy and an autocracy.
